home-no-project-recovery.scope: BROWSER-CONFIRMED LOCALISATION, 2026-09-18, on an ext4 checkout, one focused run, exit 0. This is the run the Owner's second ruling asked for, and it REPLACES the happy-dom-derived mechanism recorded before it — that one is now REFUTED. ENVIRONMENT RECIPE (reusable, and the reason every earlier browser attempt stalled): create the worktree on ext4 with `git worktree add`, then run `bun install` with BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR pointed at an ext4 directory. Do NOT rsync node_modules across the FUSE boundary; that was tried twice and never completed (15+ min, 2.8GB written, `packages/app/node_modules` and the router dist still missing). The FUSE checkout's dev server reports `ready in 220220 ms`; the ext4 one reports `ready in 834 ms` — 264x — and the same spec that wedged for hours on FUSE completes in about a minute here. Second environment fact: the app loads `@solidjs/router` through its `solid` export condition (`./dist/index.jsx` -> `dist/routers/index.js`, `dist/routing.js`, `dist/lifecycle.js`, `dist/components.jsx`), so the rollup `dist/index.js` is DEAD CODE for this app and instrumenting it produces no logs at all; the first instrumented run looked like 'the navigate path is never reached' purely because the logs were in the wrong file. ORDERED EVIDENCE from the corrected run, all one pass, timestamps in ms: `newDraft` entered with the draftID and href and the store already containing it (`storeDrafts` has the new id); `navigateFromRoute ENTERED {to:"/new-session?draftId=..."}`; `navigateFromRoute decision {resolvedTo:"/new-session?draftId=...", current:"/", referrers:0, willEnter:true}`; `beforeLeave ALLOWED`; `transition() {newIntent:"navigate", reference:"/"}` with NO early return; `transition body RAN {stillSameTarget:true}`; `setReference about to write {value:"/new-session?draftId=..."}`; `setReference written; reference() now {reference:"/new-session?draftId=..."}` — so the location signal DID take the new value and read back correctly; THEN `Routes render {browserUrl:"/"}` and `router state {url:"/", isRouting:false}` — the router's own location reads `/` again even though the write above succeeded; `finally batch started {referenceBeforeNaviEnd:"/new-session?draftId=..."}`; `navigateEnd {hasReferrer:true, referrers:1}`; `source setter {ignore:false, willWriteHistory:true}`; `Router.set`; `pushState url=/new-session?draftId=... state=null`; `replaceState url=undefined state={"_depth":2}`. THEN THE APP EMITS NOTHING EVER AGAIN: no further `Routes render`, no further `router state`, and crucially no `NATIVE EFFECT fired` — the `createRenderEffect(on(source, source => transition("native", source), {defer:true}))` callback never runs for the source write that `navigateEnd` just made, so the location signal is never re-derived from it. The surface stays absent and no error is raised. TWO CANDIDATES REFUTED BY THIS RUN, both of which the previous round left open. (1) The picker's own resource is NOT the owner: `dialog-select-directory.tsx:60-68` and `dialog-select-directory-v2.tsx:67-74` do contain the `createResource(() => (missingBase() ? true : undefined), ...)` shape that `DESIGN.md:39-43` forbids, and that was the strongest lead going in, but the instrumented resource reports `{state:"ready", loading:false, missingBase:false, syncHome:"C:/Aigcfroge", ...}` — it never even started loading, because `sync.data.path.home` was already populated by the time the picker mounted. So it holds nothing pending and it is not what freezes this navigation, even though it matches the forbidden pattern. (2) No transition is held at read time: `isRouting:false` in the same window where the location reads `/`, and no `Transition.promises`/queue symptom appears anywhere in the run, which also refutes the happy-dom-derived 'pending promise withholds promotion' mechanism this record carried before. The throw candidate is likewise unsupported: zero `pageerror`, zero console errors, no `ErrorPage`. WHAT REMAINS, stated as the current best description rather than as a root cause: the router's signal layer takes the new value during the transition and then reads `/` again while the transition is settling, and the native effect that would re-derive location from the source write never fires after `navigateEnd` commits the URL — so the app is left with a browser URL on the draft route and a router that still believes it is on `/`. That is a router-internal promotion/notification gap, not app code, and it is NOT yet pinned to a specific line: the next step is to instrument `writeSignal`/`completeUpdates` in `solid-js/dist/solid.js` around the promotion loop to see whether the source node is promoted without its observers being marked stale. NO FIX IS AUTHORISED YET and none was attempted. See `unlock` for the second instrumented round, which overturns part of the mechanism described above: no Solid transition is ever created for this navigation, so the promotion path this paragraph reasons about never runs at all.
home-no-project-recovery.unlock: SECOND INSTRUMENTED ROUND (read-only, ext4, exit 0) overturned the mechanism recorded one commit earlier and narrowed the question sharply. Instrumenting `solid-js/dist/dev.js` and `dist/solid.js` at `completeUpdates` shows `hasTransition:false` on EVERY call, including throughout the navigation and after it, with `promises`/`queue`/`sources` all null. That means NO Solid transition is ever created for this navigation: `startTransition` only builds one when `Scheduler || SuspenseContext` is truthy, and the router's `transition()` here runs from `navigateFromRoute` -> `tabs.newDraft` -> the picker callback, i.e. outside any render/Suspense context, so `SuspenseContext` is null and no Transition is constructed. CONSEQUENCES, and they matter: (a) the `setReference` write is IMMEDIATE and unbuffered, not deferred to `tValue`, so the recorded read-back of `/new-session?draftId=...` was a real value in the real slot; (b) therefore the later read of `/` by the router's own `useLocation()` is a genuine REVERT of that slot, not a deferred-promotion artifact — which RETRACTS the promotion-gap mechanism this record carried in the previous commit, along with the whole happy-dom-derived line of reasoning about `Transition.promises` withholding promotion. The question is now exactly two candidates, and both are answerable by reading code rather than by more log spam: either something writes `/` back into the location signal between the successful write and the next read, or the source signal's write in `navigateEnd` does not notify its observers (which is why `NATIVE EFFECT fired` never appears after `pushState`). NOTE for whoever picks this up: `<Navigate href="/" />` is installed as `DraftRoute`'s fallback at `app.tsx:353`, and a `<Navigate>` firing on a route that briefly resolves would write exactly `/` back — but `DraftRoute` never logged `entered` in any round, so that remains a hypothesis to test, NOT a finding. Candidates already refuted by measurement and not to be re-litigated: the picker's `fallbackPath` resource (it reported `state:"ready", loading:false, missingBase:false` — never started loading); a held transition (`isRouting:false` in the read window, and now `hasTransition:false` outright); a thrown exception (no `pageerror`, no console error, no `ErrorPage`); `DirtyDraftGuard`'s `useBeforeLeave` (the navigation reaches the browser, so nothing was prevented); and `DraftRoute`'s `tabs.ready()` gate plus `keyed` fallback ordering (all three orderings render normally in isolation).
